notes: First verdict. Checked HEAD 7fbb9e1 live on `dev.mjs --no-build --port 3311`. Strong: one fresh server per request, nothing stored, links carry data in the #fragment, 2 MB body cap, CORS, read-only annotations. Missing numbers give the exact next question (`describeNotReady`, tools.ts:214). Every step returns text, then a report link and a coaching line. What holds it back: (1) Picking the decision template (tools.ts:284-293) misroutes. "What if I hire a part-timer?" returns the lunch-deal questions and "Start by asking…". The README's "hire a part-timer for the lunch rush" counts as a good fit with no caveat, and "put my cakes down to €3" gets lunch_offer instead of price_change. (2) The server trusts state tokens. decodeState (state.ts:67) inflates with no cap: a 136 K-char token becomes a 100 MB string. The decoded business/question skip the 200/500 limits, so `cafeName`'s regex (sim/rounds.ts:80) runs in quadratic time. A 602-char token costs 5 s of CPU, and a 5 MB-padded one hung the dev server for over 2 min until I killed it. (3) The interview description and brief block tell the model to call whatif_rehearsal_submit (tools.ts:872, 895). (4) No public deployment: the README says YOUR-SITE. The stdio fallback what-if-coach.vercel.app (stdio.ts:17) returns DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND.
improvements: src/state.ts:67 and src/mcp/tools.ts:241 (decodeToken): treat a decoded token as untrusted input. Inflate with a hard output cap (e.g. 64 KB; reject anything larger). Then re-validate with the same limits the schemas use: business ≤ 200, question ≤ 500, at most 30 input keys with values ≤ 100 chars, at most 12 personas × 5 rounds of reactions, event/interview text cut to LIMITS. Also anchor or simplify the `cafeName` regex (sim/rounds.ts:80) so it is linear. Why: 'stateless and safe as a public endpoint: input limits'. Today a 602-char token burns 5 s of CPU and a slightly larger one pins a Vercel function until it times out. Done when a test sends a token whose business is padded to 5 MB and gets a plain error in under 100 ms.

src/mcp/tools.ts:284-293 (pickTemplate) and the whatif_start handler (tools.ts:471-482): stop sending lunch-deal questions for decisions What-IF cannot model. Add an 'unsupported' result for hiring, opening hours, staffing and new products. It leads with 'What-IF cannot model this decision yet', gives no 'Start by asking' line and no field list, and suggests one honest mapping, or reasoning with labelled numbers. Recognise price cuts ('down to', 'reduce', 'discount', '€3 after 4 pm') as price_change. Why: tool descriptions must make the right call obvious. §5.3's own test ('hire a part-timer') fails today, and two README examples (README.md 'Just say what if…') land on the wrong template. Done when a test table of 10 questions (the README's six plus Sunday hours, 9 pm closing, a cheaper student lunch and a coffee price rise) gets the right template or 'unsupported' for each.

src/mcp/tools.ts:872 and :895 (whatif_rehearsal_interview): the description and the brief block both append HOST_RUN_INSTRUCTIONS, which says 'then call whatif_rehearsal_submit'. Two lines later they say to call whatif_rehearsal_interview again. Make HOST_RUN_INSTRUCTIONS take the submit tool as a parameter, and pass 'whatif_rehearsal_interview with answers' here. Why: the description and the next step contradict each other. A model that follows the first sentence wastes a call, and in a running rehearsal its interview answers come back as validation errors. Done when no interview text mentions whatif_rehearsal_submit.

src/mcp/tools.ts:933-1047 and :553-583: return `state` from whatif_run_scenarios and whatif_what_changed. Let whatif_plan_test, whatif_log_result, whatif_what_changed and whatif_rehearsal_start take `state` (or a report_url) in place of template + inputs + business + question + demo + currency. Why: input schemas a model can fill. Today `whatif_plan_test {template, state}` after a demo run says '6 numbers still missing' and tells the model to ask the owner 'Roughly how many customers…' again, which is the wrong next step. Every later call must also re-send six fields correctly, demo: true included. Done when plan_test and log_result work from state alone.

src/mcp/tools.ts:172 (cleanInputs) and the check_inputs text: name unknown input keys instead of dropping them. Example: 'Ignored customers_per_day, average_spend: not fields of lunch_offer. Did you mean weekday_customers, avg_spend?' Accept rough numbers ('about 140', '~140', '140ish'), because the schema invites text. Also rewrite the damaged-token error (state.ts:73, 'ask the coach for a fresh link'): the model is the coach. Tell it to paste the state from the latest result exactly, use the report_url's #token instead, or restart with whatif_rehearsal_start. Why: errors should tell the model what to do next. Today the owner is asked again for numbers they already gave. Done when misnamed keys come back as a correction rather than as 'missing'.

src/mcp/stdio.ts:17 and README.md:29: deploy the public endpoint and put the real URL in the README, Connect page and stdio default. Until then, make the stdio fallback http://localhost:3000 rather than an unclaimed what-if-coach.vercel.app, which returns DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND. Anyone could claim that name and receive owners' report links. Why: 'a self-contained Vercel bundle' only counts when a judge can paste a URL. Judge the product as shipped. Done when `curl https://<real-site>/api/mcp` returns the info JSON and the README has no YOUR-SITE.
